expectations.text: Communication is assessed through the depth and quality of follow-up conversation, not a single scripted question.
expectations.evidence: Under Interview questions, the transcript says: "Communication. No scripted question. Score the quality of follow-up conversation across the whole loop." The competency table's Strong (4) anchor is "Follow-ups deepen the topic", and its Weak (1) anchor is "Scripted, flat". Communication is clearly scored on follow-up depth, not on one question.

expectations.text: Scorecard outcomes are measurable and specific; no vague 'run great events'-style responsibility appears.
expectations.evidence: All six outcomes have a concrete measure: show-up rate (attended ÷ RSVP) per city, share of attendees at 2+ events in 6 months, % of new joiners who post within 14 days, median time to first reply, % budget variance plus satisfaction score, and first-time speakers per quarter. No vague 'run great events' responsibility appears. The score is not 5 because none of the outcomes has a numeric target yet. Targets are deferred to "day 30 from baselines", so the outcomes are measurable but not fully specified.

expectations.evidence: Collaboration and communication (10%) is sourced from 'All blocks, bank F', so it is not tied to one question. Section 4 also gives a general follow-up instruction: 'Use follow-ups to dig for evidence (what exactly did you do, what was the number, what would you change)'. But that instruction targets evidence, not communication quality. Bank F has only two scripted prompts. The rubric never says to judge communication from how she handles back-and-forth, how deep her answers go under probing, or how clear she is in the 80–90 min Q&A. expectations.text: Scorecard outcomes are measurable and specific; no vague 'run great events'-style responsibility appears.
expectations.evidence: Most year-one outcomes have metric shapes. Examples: 'median time-to-first-answer under X hours and Y% of questions answered within 24h', 'repeat-attendee rate above X%', 'cost per attendee under $X', and 'at least N community-sourced docs or product fixes shipped, each traced to a thread'. However, every target is a placeholder (X/Y/Z/N), so none is specific yet. Outcome 7, 'a quarterly community report tied to adoption signals, no vanity metrics', is a deliverable with no measurable bar. The mission line 'running a healthy Discord' is close to the vague style the item forbids.
